```{r}
#| label: initial-setup
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Data importation
eige_raw     <- read_csv("data/wmid_natparl.csv") # Proportion of women in national parliaments
renew_raw    <- read_csv("data/nrg_ind_ren.csv") # Share of renewable energies
spend_raw    <- read_csv("data/gov_10a_exp.csv") # Public spending on environmental protection
tax_raw      <- read_csv("data/env_ac_tax.csv") # Environmental taxes
paygap_raw   <- read_csv("data/sdg_05_20.csv") # Pay gap between women and men
election_raw <- read_csv("data/view_election.csv") # Elections
party_raw    <- read_csv("data/view_party.csv") # Political parties

# Reference table of the 27 EU Member States 
eu27 <- tribble( # Manually created table with 2 columns : country name and its associated Eurostat code
  ~country,      ~code, # "~" allows to declare the column names
  "Austria",     "AT", "Belgium",    "BE", "Bulgaria",   "BG",
  "Croatia",     "HR", "Cyprus",     "CY", "Czechia",    "CZ",
  "Denmark",     "DK", "Estonia",    "EE", "Finland",    "FI",
  "France",      "FR", "Germany",    "DE", "Greece",     "EL",
  "Hungary",     "HU", "Ireland",    "IE", "Italy",      "IT",
  "Latvia",      "LV", "Lithuania",  "LT", "Luxembourg", "LU",
  "Malta",       "MT", "Netherlands","NL", "Poland",     "PL",
  "Portugal",    "PT", "Romania",    "RO", "Slovakia",   "SK",
  "Slovenia",    "SI", "Spain",      "ES", "Sweden",     "SE"
)
```

# Data sources

## How to obtain the data

The table below gives for each source: the link to the data, the filters used, and the download date.

For Eurostat, we opened the table in the Eurostat Data Browser, applied the filters listed below, and exported the result as a CSV file. EIGE (a CSV file) and ParlGov
(a ZIP archive of CSV tables) were downloaded in full. The selection of the variables and period used in the analysis is described in the data cleaning section.

| Source | Data | Filters at download | Download date |
|---|---|---|---|
| EIGE | [wmid_natparl](https://eige.europa.eu/gender-statistics/dgs/indicator/wmidm_pol_parl__wmid_natparl) | None (full table downloaded). | 2026-10-22 |
| Eurostat | [nrg_ind_ren](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/nrg_ind_ren/default/table?lang=en) | `nrg_bal` = REN, `unit` = PC, `geo` = the 27 EU Member States, from 2004. | 2026-10-22 |
| Eurostat | [gov_10a_exp](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/gov_10a_exp/default/table) | `sector` = S13, `cofog99` = GF05, `na_item` = TE, `unit` = PC_GDP, `geo` = the 27 EU Member States, from 2004. | 2026-10-22 |
| Eurostat | [env_ac_tax](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/env_ac_tax/default/table) | `unit` = PC_GDP, `geo` = the 27 EU Member States, from 2004 (all tax types). | 2026-10-22 |
| Eurostat | [sdg_05_20](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/sdg_05_20/default/table?lang=en) | `nace_r2` = B-S_X_O, `unit` = PC, `geo` = the 27 EU Member States, all years (2007–2022). | 2026-11-17 |
| ParlGov | [parlgov.org](https://parlgov.org/data-info/) | None (full archive downloaded, November 2023 version). | 2026-10-23 |

## Description of the sources

**EIGE.** The European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE) is an EU agency. Its Gender Statistics Database collects data on the number of women and men in decision-making positions. The table "National parliaments: presidents and members" (*wmid_natparl*) counts women and men among the members and the presidents of national parliaments, for the single or lower house, the upper house and both houses combined. It is a quarterly data set covering `r n_distinct(eige_raw$geo)` countries and aggregates, from `r substr(min(eige_raw$time), 1, 4)` to `r substr(max(eige_raw$time), 1, 4)`. Each row corresponds to a combination of country, quarter, chamber, position, sex and unit (absolute number or percentage). The share of women in the single or lower house is our explanatory variable.

**Eurostat.** Eurostat is the statistical office of the European Union, and its data are harmonized across Member States. We used four annual data sets: 

- *nrg_ind_ren* : share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption, the indicator used to express the EU targets for 2020 and 2030. It measures the outcome of environmental policies.
- *gov_10a_exp* : general government expenditure by function (COFOG classification), here on environmental protection, as a percentage of GDP. It measures the budgetary effort. 
- *env_ac_tax* : environmental tax revenues from national accounts, by category (energy, transport, pollution and resources), as a percentage of GDP. It measures a fiscal instrument voted by parliaments. 

- *sdg_05_20* : unadjusted gender pay gap, defined as the difference between the average gross hourly earnings of men and women, as a percentage of men's earnings. It covers firms with ten employees or more, in industry, construction and services (except public administration, defense and compulsory social security). It is based on the Structure of Earnings Survey, which takes place every four years, with national estimates for the years in between. 

**ParlGov.** ParlGov (Parliaments and Governments database) is an academic database compiled from official and secondary sources. It documents elections, parties and cabinets in European and OECD democracies. The version used here is the November 2023 archive, made of 33 CSV tables. We used two of them: 

- *view_election* : number of seats won by each party at each election. 
- *view_party* : political family of each party. 

Combined, they give the share of seats held by green parties, our second control variable.

## Data files

```{r}
#| label: file-tables
#| results: asis

# Build one table per data file.
# d: the data frame
# file: its path
# content: short description
# time: the column with dates (NULL if none)
# area: the column with countries

file_info <- function(d, file, content, time = NULL, area) {
  tibble(
    Item  = c("File", "Content", "Rows", "Columns", "Period", "Countries / entities"),
    Value = c(file, content,
              format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), # number of rows
              ncol(d), # number of columns
              if (is.null(time)) "Not applicable" else paste(range(substr(time, 1, 4)), collapse = " to "), # first and last year of the data 
              n_distinct(area)) # number of different countries
  )
}

# Store each table in a list.   
tables <- list(
  "EIGE: women in national parliaments" =
    file_info(eige_raw, "data/wmid_natparl.csv",
              "Number or percentage of women and men in national parliaments, by quarter",
              eige_raw$time, eige_raw$geo),
  "Eurostat: renewable energy share" =
    file_info(renew_raw, "data/nrg_ind_ren.csv",
              "Share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption (%)",
              renew_raw$TIME_PERIOD, renew_raw$geo),
  "Eurostat: government spending on environmental protection" =
    file_info(spend_raw, "data/gov_10a_exp.csv",
              "General government expenditure on environmental protection (% of GDP)",
              spend_raw$TIME_PERIOD, spend_raw$geo),
  "Eurostat: environmental taxes" =
    file_info(tax_raw, "data/env_ac_tax.csv",
              "Environmental tax revenues (% of GDP)",
              tax_raw$TIME_PERIOD, tax_raw$geo),
  "Eurostat: gender pay gap" =
    file_info(paygap_raw, "data/sdg_05_20.csv",
              "Unadjusted gender pay gap (% of men's hourly earnings)",
              paygap_raw$TIME_PERIOD, paygap_raw$geo),
  "ParlGov: election results" =
    file_info(election_raw, "data/view_election.csv",
              "Seats won by each party at each election",
              election_raw$election_date, election_raw$country_name),
  "ParlGov: parties" =
    file_info(party_raw, "data/view_party.csv",
              "Political family of each party",
              area = party_raw$country_name)
)

# Print the tables one after the other.
for (i in seq_along(tables)) {
  title <- names(tables)[i]
  if (i > 1) cat("\n\n&nbsp;")   # blank line between a table and the next title
  cat("\n\n**", sub(":.*", "", title), "**:", sub("^[^:]*:", "", title), "\n\n", sep = "") # title in bold, the rest in normal font
  cat(kable(tables[[i]]), sep = "\n") # kable() turns the tibble into a markdown table, cat() writes it in the document
}
```
